implementation_notes: Python has no nominal interfaces, so LSP/ISP must be declared explicitly with `typing.Protocol` (structural subtyping) and checked with a type checker. Use `typing.Protocol` for the DIP seam, keep it in the consuming module, and validate with `@runtime_checkable` or `isinstance` when the boundary crosses a process boundary.
idiom_name: typing.Protocol (structural interface) + ABC where nominal behaviour is needed
pitfalls: Using `abc.ABC` in the implementing package makes the dependency point the wrong way for DIP.
Protocols with many methods quietly become fat interfaces; split them per consumer.
Duck typing without any declared Protocol means type checkers cannot verify substitutability.
Monkey-patching a class from another module is a global LSP violation.
